title: Cards inside cards, everything in a rounded box
use_when: Reviewing any layout where sections, lists, forms, and even single lines are wrapped in bordered/elevated containers.
avoid_when: A card is fine when the item is a discrete tappable object or needs elevation (drag, overlay).
guidance: Justify each container: does the boundary mean something (tappable object, elevation, grouping that spacing cannot express)? If not, replace with headings, spacing, and hairline dividers. Never nest a card in a card; never wrap a single KPI number in a card just to make a grid.

title: Purple/blue gradients and gradient blobs by default
use_when: Any background, hero, button, or KPI tile with a gradient that the brand did not ask for.
avoid_when: Gradients earn their place when they encode depth/scrim, are part of the brand's defined system, or are used once as a signature.
guidance: Remove decorative gradients unless the brand system defines them; particularly indigo→violet→pink, radial blobs behind heroes, and gradient text. Use solid tokens; if a gradient stays, define it as a token with a stated purpose and verify text contrast at both ends.
source: Observed AI-generated UI patterns; Anthropic frontend-design calibration

title: Glassmorphism without a reason
use_when: Frosted panels, blurred cards, translucent nav bars in application UI.
avoid_when: Platform materials for transient layers (sheets, menus) are legitimate.
guidance: Replace with solid tonal surfaces unless the layer must reveal content beneath it; if kept, use the platform material, verify contrast against worst-case backgrounds, and measure GPU cost on low-end devices and TV.

title: Pills for everything
use_when: Pill-shaped buttons, inputs, nav items, badges, and tags all at once; pill badges on every list item.
avoid_when: Pills are right for filters/tags, compact status, segmented controls.
guidance: Pick one corner language for controls (small/medium radius) and reserve full-round for chips/badges; ≤2 badges per item; buttons and inputs share a radius; if everything is a pill, nothing reads as a tag.

title: Decorative icon next to every heading/feature
use_when: Feature grids with an icon in a tinted circle above each title, list items with a random icon each, headings with emoji.
avoid_when: Icons that disambiguate (file type, status, action) are fine.
guidance: Remove icons that don't carry meaning; never use emoji as UI icons; if a feature grid needs visuals, use real product imagery or none. Icon count on a screen should track the number of distinct actions/states, not the number of headings.

title: Identical landing skeleton (hero + 3 features + testimonials + CTA)
use_when: Any landing page whose structure could belong to any other product: centred headline, gradient subtitle, two buttons, floating screenshot, three-column icon features, logo wall, testimonial carousel, pricing, FAQ, CTA.
avoid_when: Some of these sections are right for some products; the problem is the fixed sequence regardless of product.
guidance: Derive the page structure from what convinces this product's buyer: a live demo, a calculator, a comparison table, a single case study, the actual data, a photograph of the physical thing. Cut sections that only exist because the template has them. The section order is a decision, state it.
source: Observed AI-generated UI patterns; frontend-design skill

title: Oversized display text and 'big number' KPIs everywhere
use_when: 72–96 px headlines on app screens, KPI tiles with 48 px numbers and tiny labels, everything bold.
avoid_when: A single large focal number is fine when it is the screen's one thing.
guidance: Reserve display sizes for one element per screen; app headings 20–28 px; KPI value 24–32 px with a readable label; hierarchy comes from contrast between roles, not from making everything large. TV is the exception with its own scale.

title: The default SaaS dashboard (sidebar + 4 KPI cards + chart + table)
use_when: Any 'dashboard' request answered with the same skeleton regardless of what the user monitors or does.
avoid_when: Each element can be right; the failure is choosing them before knowing the task.
guidance: Start from the user's job: what decision or action happens here, how often, and what must be noticed first. Many 'dashboards' should be a table-first working screen, a queue, or a single chart with alerts. Choose navigation by section count, KPIs by decisions, charts by questions. If the result is a sidebar and four KPIs, be able to say why.

title: Choosing a visual style before understanding product, user, and platform
use_when: Any request answered with 'glassmorphism + purple gradient + Inter' (or any style) before asking who uses it, where, with what input, at what density.
avoid_when: When the user explicitly specifies the style, follow it, but still check platform fit.
guidance: Order of decisions: task and user → environment and input → density and navigation → layout → components → then type, colour, surface, motion. Visual style is downstream of structure. Record the KNOWN/INFERRED/MISSING ledger before choosing a look.

title: Trend aesthetics at the cost of usability
use_when: Low-contrast grey-on-grey text, neumorphic controls with no affordance, brutalist forms with no labels, bento grids for tabular data, ultra-thin fonts on TV.
avoid_when: A trend can be used when it survives the accessibility and platform checks.
guidance: Run every aesthetic choice through contrast, target size, focus visibility, platform input model, and reading distance before keeping it. Brand character must come from choices that pass, not from breaking them.

title: Scroll-triggered reveals on every section, parallax by default
use_when: Fade-up on every heading, staggered cards on scroll, parallax backgrounds, floating orbs.
avoid_when: One orchestrated moment can be right.
guidance: Motion must communicate hierarchy, continuity, feedback, or state; decorative scroll animation slows reading and marks the page as generated. Keep at most one reveal sequence, honour reduced motion, and never animate layout properties.

title: A desktop or mobile layout enlarged for TV
use_when: TV screens with hover menus, small links, scrollbars, sidebars with 12 items, forms with many fields, hamburger menus, touch gestures, mouse-oriented layouts.
avoid_when: Never.
guidance: Rebuild around focus: rails and grids, side/top navigation, one visible focus, 10-foot type scale, safe margins, minimal text entry, transport controls, BACK semantics. Reuse data and business logic, not the layout.
source: Android TV design principles; tvOS HIG

title: Desktop screen shrunk to a phone
use_when: Tables with horizontal scroll as the primary view, 12-px labels, sidebars turned into hamburger menus with 20 items, hover-only actions, dense toolbars.
avoid_when: Never.
guidance: Re-prioritise for the phone's tasks: fewer things, bigger targets, bottom-anchored actions, list rows instead of tables, sheets instead of side panels, platform navigation grammar.

title: Brands that differ only by logo, primary colour, and font
use_when: Multi-brand or white-label products where every brand shares navigation, layout, density, card geometry, imagery, and CTA behaviour.
avoid_when: Shared structure is acceptable when brands are explicitly meant to be the same product with a skin; then say so.
guidance: Run fingerprint.py compare on the candidate brand systems; a COSMETIC-ONLY verdict fails differentiation. Vary at least two structural axes (navigation model, layout topology, density, surface strategy, image strategy, metadata density, CTA strategy) per brand, then cosmetics.

title: Arbitrary spacing and misaligned edges
use_when: Paddings like 13/18/22 px, cards with different inner padding, text not aligned to the grid, icons off-baseline, unequal gaps between equal items.
avoid_when: Never.
guidance: Snap every value to the spacing scale, align left edges of text across components, use one inset per container type, check icon/text baseline alignment, and equalise gaps in repeated structures. This single fix does more for 'looks professional' than any colour change.

title: Default type choices (Inter/Roboto everywhere, Space Grotesk on every startup)
use_when: Brand-led surfaces where the type was chosen by habit rather than for the brief.
avoid_when: Functional tools and native apps may legitimately use system/neutral fonts; the codebase's existing font wins unless the task is to change it.
guidance: When type carries identity, choose from the brief (subject, audience, tone), verify coverage/figures/weights, and avoid the current AI default clusters (cream+serif+terracotta; near-black+acid accent; Space Grotesk/Inter for everything).
source: Anthropic frontend-design skill calibration; observed patterns

title: Dark mode by inversion
use_when: Pure black canvas with pure white text, saturated light-theme accents on dark, shadows that vanish, borders that disappear, images unchanged.
avoid_when: Never.
guidance: Redesign surfaces (elevation = lighter), desaturate accents, use 87/60/38% white text steps, re-validate every pair, define dark chart palettes. See the dark mode rule.
source: Material dark theme; Apple dark mode

title: Actions only on hover
use_when: Row actions, card menus, and edit buttons that appear only on mouse hover.
avoid_when: Never as the sole path.
guidance: Show on focus too, keep a visible affordance (overflow menu) for touch, and never on TV.

title: Placeholder as the only label
use_when: Inputs whose label disappears on typing; low-contrast placeholder text.
avoid_when: Never.
guidance: Visible persistent label (above or floating with a real label element), placeholder only for format hints, placeholder contrast ≥4.5:1.

title: Only the happy state was designed
use_when: Screens with no empty, loading, error, offline, partial, or long-text states; buttons with no pressed/disabled/loading states; TV cards with no focused state.
avoid_when: Never.
guidance: Enumerate states per screen and per interactive component before implementation and verify each visually; test with long strings, zero items, 10k items, and slow networks.

title: Interruptive upsells and promo banners
use_when: Modal upsells on launch, banners that push content down after load, 'upgrade' interstitials in task flows, undismissable promos.
avoid_when: A single dismissible, non-blocking promotion in a clearly marked area is acceptable.
guidance: Never block a task with a promotion; place promos in reserved space so content does not shift; make them dismissible with a persistent memory of the dismissal; keep them out of the DPAD/keyboard path on TV and desktop (not the first focus); never mimic system dialogs or error styling; cap frequency. On shared or public screens keep promotional copy non-personal.
source: Dark-pattern research (Brignull); Core Web Vitals CLS
